definitions.explanation: A town that developed around a port or harbor, typically associated with maritime trade, fishing, and a distinctive coastal atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {横浜|よこはま}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{港町|みなとまち}だ。
examples.english: Yokohama is a famous port town.

examples.japanese: {港町|みなとまち}には{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}を{出|だ}す{店|みせ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Port towns have many restaurants that serve fresh fish.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さな{港町|みなとまち}を{散歩|さんぽ}していると、{潮|しお}の{香|かお}りがして{気持|きも}ちがよかった。
examples.english: Walking around the small port town, the scent of the sea was pleasant.

notes:
USAGE:
{港町|みなとまち} is a compound of {港|みなと} (port/harbor) and {町|まち} (town). Japan has many famous port towns including {横浜|よこはま}, {神戸|こうべ}, {長崎|ながさき}, and {函館|はこだて}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {港町|みなとまち}を{歩|ある}く (walk around a port town)
- {港町|みなとまち}の{風情|ふぜい} (the charm of a port town)
- {港町|みなとまち}で{育|そだ}つ (grow up in a port town)

Port towns in Japan are often associated with foreign cultural influences due to their history as points of international trade. {港町|みなとまち} evokes images of seafood, ocean views, and a blend of Japanese and Western architecture.
